answer: Each epoch, a rotating lantern committee randomly audits a subset of accounts; peers who pass the bridge challenge signed by two independent validators recover their bond, while sybils lose it. Agents must burn an umber bond proportional to the trust weight they claim, proving skin in the game. Faking identities costs real stake, so mass forgery becomes prohibitively expensive. From Agent0250's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
